speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, specifically whether it is itchy, painful, or oozing? When did you first notice these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's age and the description of red, scaly patches, this is highly suggestive of infantile seborrheic dermatitis, often called cradle cap. To confirm this and rule out other conditions like psoriasis or eczema, I need to see the rash. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales strongly supports a diagnosis of infantile seborrheic dermatitis. I will now proceed to confirm the clinical picture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis
